rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is framed with an implied saying: God tells Moses, “Go to Pharaoh.”
rows.anchor: على ارادة القول ﴿ إنه طغى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh exceeded the bounds through unbelief and corruption.
rows.anchor: تجاوز الحد فى الكفر والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invitation asks whether Pharaoh is inclined to purify himself from idolatry and disobedience through obedience and faith.
rows.anchor: هل لك ميل إلى أن تتطهر من الشرك والعصيان بالطاعة والإيمان

rows.speaker: حجازى
rows.claim: A Hijazi reading geminates the zāy in تزكى.
rows.anchor: العصيان بالطاعة والإيمان وبتشديد الزاى حجازى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses offers to guide Pharaoh to knowledge of God by recounting His attributes, so Pharaoh may know Him.
rows.anchor: وأرشدك إلى معرفة الله بذكر صفاته فتعرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of God only comes through knowledge of Him, as the Qur'an says that those who fear God among His servants are the learned.
rows.anchor: لأن الخشية لا تكون إلا بالمعرفة قال الله تعالى إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء

rows.speaker: بعض الحكماء
rows.claim: A sage says that whoever knows God cannot disobey Him even for an instant.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض الحكماء اعرف الله فمن عرف الله لم يقدر أن يعصيه طرفة عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is the basis of conduct: fearing God brings every good, while feeling secure leads one to dare every evil.
rows.anchor: فالخشية ملاك الأمر من خشى الله أتى منه كل خير ومن أمن من اجترأ على كل شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that whoever fears sets out by night, and whoever sets out by night reaches his destination.
rows.anchor: ومنه لحديث من خاف أدلج ومن أدلج بلغ المنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses begins with an interrogative invitation, like a host gently asking a guest to stay.
rows.anchor: بدأ مخاطبته بالاستفهام الذى معناه العرض كما يقول الرجل لضيفه هل لك أن تنزل بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He follows with gentle speech to attract Pharaoh kindly and coax him away from arrogance, in keeping with the command to speak softly to him.
rows.anchor: واردفه الكلام الرقيق ليستدعيه باللطف فى القول ويستنزله بالمداراة عن عتوة كما أمر بذلك فى قوله تعالى فقولا له قولا لينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh denied Moses and the great sign, called Moses a sorcerer and the sign sorcery, and disobeyed God.
rows.anchor: فرعون بموسى والآية الكبرى وسماها ساحرا وسحرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh turned away from Moses.
rows.anchor: ﴾ تولى عن موسى ﴿ يسعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Pharaoh strove to plot against Moses.
rows.anchor: ﴾ يجتهد فى مكايدته أو لما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, on seeing the serpent he fled in terror, hurrying along because he was rash and impulsive.
rows.anchor: لما راى الثعبان أدبر مرعوبا يسرع فى مشيته وكان طياشا خفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh gathered the magicians and his troops.
rows.anchor: ﴾ فجمع السحرة وجنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He called out at the place where those gathered with him had assembled.
rows.anchor: فى إلى مقام الذى اجتمعوا فيه معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nakal means making an example of someone, as salām means giving peace.
rows.anchor: والنكال بمعنى التنكيل كالسلام بمعنى التسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative is a cognate accusative because “seizing” here has the sense of “punishing”: God punished him with a punishment.
rows.anchor: ونصبه على المصدر لأن أخذ بمعنى نكل كأنه قيل نكل الله به نكال الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes the punishment as burning, the punishment of the Hereafter, and the earlier punishment as drowning.
rows.anchor: أى الاحراق ﴿ والأولى ﴾ أى الاغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the punishment answers Pharaoh's two claims: “I am your highest lord” and “I know no god for you but me”; Nasafi gives forty, thirty, or twenty years between them.
rows.anchor: أو نكال كلمتيه الآخرة وهى أنا ربكم الأعلى والأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “As for” answers the earlier “when”; when the overwhelming calamity comes, the matter is as described.
rows.anchor: جواب فإذا أى إذا جاءت الطامة فإن الأمر كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressor is one who crosses the limit and disbelieves.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من طغى ﴾ جاوز الحد فكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers worldly life to the Hereafter by following his desires.
rows.anchor: ﴾ على الآخرة باتباع الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is the place of return.
rows.anchor: هي المأوى ﴾ المرجع أى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He contrasts this with the abode of the one who fears his Lord's standing and restrains his soul from desire.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى ﴿ سورة عبس

rows.speaker: الكوفيين
rows.claim: The Kufans take the definite article as a substitute for a possessive construction.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام بدل من الاضافة وهذا عند الكوفيين

rows.speaker: سيبويه والبصريين
rows.claim: Sibawayh and the Basrans understand it as “the place of refuge for him.”
rows.anchor: وعند سيبويه وعند البصريين هى المأوى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Because he came” is accusative as a purpose clause; grammarians differ over whether its governor is عبس or تولى.
rows.anchor: ومحله نصب لأنه مفعول له والعامل فيه عبس أو تولى على اختلاف المذهبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind man is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm; Umm Maktūm is his mother, and his father was Abū Shurayḥ ibn Mālik.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وام مكتوم أم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum came while the Prophet was inviting Quraysh leaders to Islam and repeatedly asked to be taught, unaware of the Prophet's preoccupation; the Prophet frowned and turned away, occasioning the revelation. Afterwards he honored him, welcomed him as the one for whom his Lord reproached him, and appointed him deputy over Medina twice.
rows.anchor: أتى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يدعو أشراف قريش إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who considers himself self-sufficient is wealthy in money.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أما من استغنى ﴾ أى منكان غنيا بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: You turn your attention toward him, eager for him to believe.
rows.anchor: تتعرض بالاقبال عليه حرصا على إيمانه

rows.speaker: حجازى
rows.claim: A Hijazi reading assimilates the tāʾ into the ṣād in تصدى.
rows.anchor: بالاقبال عليه حرصا على إيمانه تصدى بادغام التاء فى الصاد حجازى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are noble in God's sight, or noble through abstaining from sins.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كرام ﴾ على الله أو عن المعاصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bararah means pious ones and is the plural of bārr.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بررة ﴾ أتقياء جمع بار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase curses the unbelieving human being.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قتل الإنسان ﴾ لعن الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the human being is identified as Umayya or ʿUtba.
rows.anchor: أو هو أمية أو عتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an interrogative rebuke, asking what has led him to disbelief.
rows.anchor: استفهام توبيخ أى أى شىء جمله على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is an exclamation at the intensity of his disbelief.
rows.anchor: أوهو تعجب أى ما أشد كفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means “from what lowly thing was he created?” and serves to affirm his humble origin before the next verse answers.
rows.anchor: من أى حقير خلقه وهو استفهام ومعناه التقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created him from a drop and proportioned him according to what He willed for his creation.
rows.anchor: ﴾ على ما يشاء من خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A spring” is accusative either as a circumstantial expression or as an accusative of praise.
rows.anchor: ﴿ عينا ﴾ حال أو نصب على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that they drink from it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يشرب بها ﴾ أى منها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd say the close ones drink it unmixed, while it is blended for the companions of the right.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود رضى الله عنهم يشربها المقربون صرفا وتمزج لأصحاب اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since each soul has a watcher, reflection on human origins shows that the Creator can resurrect and requite him; one should work for Judgment Day and dictate only what will please the recorder in the end.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر أن على كل نفس حافظا أمره بالنظر فى أول أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an interrogative asking from what thing man was created; its answer follows in the next verse.
rows.anchor: ومم خلق استفهام أى من أى شئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāfiq describes forceful pouring; strictly the person is the one who pours, so attributing the action to the fluid is figurative.
rows.anchor: والدفق صب فيه دفع والدفق فى الحقيقة لصاحبه والاسناد إلى الماء مجاز

rows.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Some linguists say dafaqt al-māʾ means “I poured the water,” while dafaqa al-māʾ bi-nafsihi means “the water flowed.”
rows.anchor: وعن بعض أهل اللغة دفقت الماء دفقا صببته ودفق الماء بنفسه أى انصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses singular “water,” not two waters, because the fluids mingle in the womb and unite when human creation begins.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل من ماءين لا متزاجهما فى الرحم واتحادهما حين ابتدئ فى خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Creator, understood from the preceding mention of creation; the verse means the One who first created man from a drop.
rows.anchor: إن الخالق لدلالة خلق عليه ومعناه ان الذى خلق الإنسان إبتداء من نظفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His return means bringing man back to life, and the Creator is plainly able to do so and cannot be thwarted.
rows.anchor: على إعادته خصوصا ﴿ لقادر ﴾ لبين القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's “return” is rain, so named because it comes back each time.
rows.anchor: أى المطر وسمى به لعوده كل حين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's splitting is the emergence of vegetation from it.
rows.anchor: هو ما تتصدع عنه الأرض من النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening praise describes God as beyond imaginative indication and rational comprehension, eternal beyond created limits, and uniquely divine before and after all that exists.
rows.anchor: المنزه بذاته عن إشارة الأوهام المقدس بصفاته عن إدراك العقول والأفهام المتصف بالألوهية قبل كل موجود الباقي بالنعوت السرمدية بعد كل محدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is unlike created beings, bodies, and humanity, does not occupy space, and is powerful and sovereign beyond challenge.
rows.anchor: القديم الذي تعالى عن مماثلة الحدثان العظيم الذى تنزه عن مماسة المكان المتعالى عن مضاهاة الأجسام ومشابهة الأنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preface praises God as all-knowing, creator and teacher of humanity, and wise in revealing the Qur'an as a cure for souls and bodies.
rows.anchor: العليم الذي خلق الانسان وعلمه البيان الحكيم الذى نزل القرآن شفاء للأرواح والأبدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At a request, al-Nasafī says he wrote a moderate tafsir integrating grammar, readings, rhetorical subtleties, and allusions, presenting Sunni views and excluding innovators' doctrines.
rows.anchor: كتابا وسطا في التأويلات جامعا لوجوه الاعراب والقراءات متضمنا لدقائق علمى البديع والاشارات حاليا بأقاويل أهل السنة والجماعة خاليا عن أباطيل أهل البدع والضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says he hesitated from awareness of human limits and caution, then completed the work quickly with God's aid and titled it Madārik al-tanzīl wa-ḥaqāʾiq al-taʾwīl.
rows.anchor: وكنت أقدم فيه رجلا وأؤخر أخرى استقصارا لقوة البشر عن درك هذا الوطر
